description: CRAWDAD, the Community Resource for Archiving Wireless Data, began in 2004 at Dartmouth College as a place to share wireless network data from real networks and real mobile users, and since summer 2022 has been housed on IEEE DataPort. Its datasets include Wi-Fi association and syslog traces of campus networks, cellular and CDMA measurements, Bluetooth and contact traces between people, mobility traces of taxis and buses, signal-strength surveys, and 5G testbed monitoring such as EURECOM's ElasticMon 5G, each with a DOI and a versioned name such as crawdad-dartmouthcampus. Coverage: mostly campuses, cities and testbeds in North America, Europe and Asia, 2000s onwards. Format and access: text, CSV and pcap files per dataset, open access on IEEE DataPort free of charge with a free IEEE account, under each dataset's licence (mostly Creative Commons Attribution). Caveats: each dataset is a separate study with its own method; many are old and small; anonymisation limits linking to locations. Simulation uses: user mobility and contact models, wireless network load and failure studies, and validation of agent-based models of communication during emergencies. Related records: the MIT Reality Mining and Telecom Italia datasets are other mobile traces; RIPE Atlas covers wide-area measurement.
